messages:
Anna (Support Lead): FYI customer C-9182 reporting sudden quality drop + 502s after our standby region took traffic. They say responses are truncated, weird tokenization, and a billing spike. Escalating — need triage.
Raj (Oncall): Can you paste a sample request_id and the time window? I’ll pull the routing logs. Also: are they on dedicated or hosted?

Anna (Support Lead): Hosted, EU region primary. sample_request_id=rq_0a9f3c2b, seen ~2026-03-16T14:12:10Z. Customer reports outputs with weird spacing and partial tokens like "▁the" and unexpected language switches. They got a 502 for a few requests then resumed but with degraded outputs.
Elaine (Runtime Eng): grabbing logs now. Quick question: did we recently push any standby pool config in eu-west-2?

DeployBot: [route-failover] 2026-03-16T14:11:58Z selected_pool=eu-standby-1 assigned_host=host-47 selected_model=redwood-lite-v1-q8 expected_model=redwood-base-1.3 selected_tokenizer=lite-vocab-v2 expected_tokenizer=base-vocab-v6
DeployBot: [autoscaler] 2026-03-16T14:12:00Z triggered_scale_up standby_pool=eu-standby-1 reason=region_outage_primary

Raj (Oncall): ok that log line jumps out — selected_model != expected_model. Does standby pool have differently labeled variants?

Elaine (Runtime Eng): Looks like standby pool has legacy pinned variants for lower-cost capacity (lite-v1-q8). Those are compatible from a graph of shapes but use a different tokenizer (lite-vocab) and produce byte-pair variants leading to observed tokenization artifacts. I’m seeing rewriter:failure entries for rq_0a9f3c2b referencing tokenizer mismatch. Snippet:
```
ERROR runtime: tokenizer mismatch: expected_checksum=3f5a token_map=base-v6 actual_checksum=9b2c token_map=lite-v2
request_id=rq_0a9f3c2b
```

Anna (Support Lead): Customer also attached prompt + failing response — they’re blocking invoices until we clarify and want a repro for their legal team.
Oliver (Product): Is this a config drift between pools (tokenizer metadata missing) or a planned variant mix? If it's the former we need a hotfix to prevent cross-variant routing.

Elaine (Runtime Eng): It’s config drift. The standby pool was created from an older snapshot and we didn’t sync tokenizer metadata tags. Routing policy checks only model architecture and size, not tokenizer checksum. Quick mitigation: pin that customer's account to `eu-primary` via routing override, and add a safety check rejecting model variants without matching tokenizer checksum.
Raj (Oncall): To be concrete — I can apply an account-level route override. Command:
```
curl -X POST "$ADMIN_API/pinning" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"account":"acct_9182","region":"eu-primary","force":true}'
```
Will that stop the immediate bleed?

Anna (Support Lead): Please do. I’ll tell the customer we’ve pinned them and are investigating. Also they reported a billing delta +$210 for 14:12–14:20 window.

DeployBot: [audit] 2026-03-16T14:13:05Z change=pin created_by=raj reason="customer urgent" target=acct_9182

Elaine (Runtime Eng): After pin: monitor logs for rq_0a9f3c2b family. Next steps: (1) add tokenizer_checksum to the model compatibility check in router (2) schedule backfill to update standby pool metadata (3) run a verification job across standby pools. I can draft the PR for (1) now.
Oliver (Product): Agreed. We should also consider an autoscaler policy change: avoid picking reduced-capability variants for failovers where tokenizer mismatch risk is non-trivial. Add safety-tier tag so standby variants with different vocab get lower preference.

Raj (Oncall): Mitigation applied and verified — customer traffic now routed to eu-primary. No new 502s reported for 10m. I’ve left the override in place until we confirm backfill.

Anna (Support Lead): Customer notified; they want a short RCA and ETA. Please estimate timeline for code fix + metadata sync (Elaine)?

Elaine (Runtime Eng): Code fix PR (router check) — 2–3 business days including tests. Metadata sync job — depends on pool size, estimate 4–6 hours with rollout. I’ll queue the verification job and start the PR today.

Oliver (Product): Thanks. Action items for this thread: announce pin + refund plan to customer, prioritize router checksum check, backfill standby metadata, add postmortem and follow-up with billing.

Anna (Support Lead): I'll draft a customer-facing note. Thanks team — please paste links to PR & runbook here once available. :pray:

Raj (Oncall): adding runbook entry: "standby-tokenizer-mismatch" and a short checklist: verify tokenizer checksum, pin account, escalate to runtime.
Elaine (Runtime Eng): PR: incoming -> will paste link when CI passes. Runbook updates + verification results will follow.
Anna (Support Lead): Marking resolved for now (customer confirmed temporary fix). Moving to postmortem channel after PR.
